text:
nora: heads up, seeing sustained mem growth on dedicated pool A when long-context chat sessions hit ~120k tokens. KV cache keeps climbing and eventually OOMs the worker GPU container.

samir: can you paste pmap/`nvidia-smi` snapshot? curious if it's host ram or gpu vram starving first.

nora: attached quick paste: 
```
1749004321 nora@host:~$ pmap -x 12345 | tail -n 5
total  133428 kB
26G   26843545600K  ???
```
and `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` shows steady GPU mem at ~85% then jumps to 99% when the process swaps pages.

jia: sounds similar to the VPC Dedicated incident last month but that was kernel cgroup vs runc page reclaim. This one is on our colo box (private) with a100s and `mellanox` NIC. different networking profile.

leo: important detail: the request batching heuristics changed in the canary last week (batch window from 6ms -> 12ms). That increases simultaneous KV allocations because more concurrent tokens are in-flight for the same model frame.

nora: right — with the larger batch window we observe bigger per-request KV reservations. The runtime picks the 'fast-int8' kernel for short-seq but a fallback 'stable-fp16' path for long-seq; kernel selection seems to influence page residency.

samir: do we have perf profile showing pagefault hotspot and which kernel routine? `perf script`/`perf top` maybe.

nora: ran a quick perf, here's the top stack sample (trimmed):
```
perf top samples:
  22.1% kv_cache_insert
  18.3% llc_miss_handler
  15.0% kernel_page_fault
  10.4% attention_kern_fast_int8
  6.2% attention_kern_stable_fp16
```
Suggests more page faults when fast_int8 path active.

jia: hypothesis: fast_int8 uses more small allocations (fragmentation) and touches memory pages unpredictably, while stable_fp16 preallocates big contiguous frames (fewer page faults). On our private rack with hugepages disabled, that causes scatter and reclaim thrash.

leo: if true, Dedicated cloud hosts (with our default kernel config) have transparent hugepages enabled; Hosted pool nodes have modified vm.swappiness and tuned vm.vfs_cache_pressure. Private on-prem we left defaults. Could be config drift.

samir: can we scope reproducer? steps to repro: long chat (120k tokens) using model X, canary batching enabled, pinned to fast-int8 kernel. Run under `taskset` to ensure single NUMA, and monitor `/proc/vmstat`, `perf`, and `pagemap`.

nora: I ran a lighter repro on private rack: 3 sessions @ longctx size ~80k tokens over 6 minutes, batch window 12ms. Observed gradual host RSS growth and then a ~2s stall where kernel reclaims pages -> 2 containers report OOM-kills (OOM killer targeted the executor).

jia: interesting — were these in the same NUMA domain? onprem A100 boxes commonly have NVLINK and multiple NUMA regions. If allocations end up cross-numa, page return latencies blow up.

leo: action items:
- nora: capture full `perf record -a -g` during the repro and upload flame; include `perf mem` if possible.
- samir: try toggling batch window back to 6ms for canary and run same repro on dedicated and hosted to compare.
- jia: check kernel config differences: transparent hugepages, vm.swappiness, THP compaction, and hugetlbfs usage across our images.
- ops-bot: create incident ticket and attach logs (auto).

ops-bot: created INC-2026-kv-longctx-hosted-vs-private-1749004321, priority P2, linked to eng-runtime.

nora: one more datapoint — on hosted we saw stable behavior even with 12ms because their kernel compaction path reduces fragmentation before the KV allocator hits it. So this feels like two factors: batching->allocator pattern and kernel/hardware differences.

samir: reminds me to think about runtime-level mitigation: we could force allocator to pre-reserve contiguous slab for long-context requests when kernel lacks THP. Cheap mitigation: detect longctx and switch batch window to smaller or switch to stable_fp16 kernel.

jia: agree. we should also add a short diagnostic at runtime that logs kernel config: /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled, vm.swappiness, numa maps, and NIC offload flags on startup for each node type. Helps detect config drift between pools.

leo: will prototype: longctx flag -> (a) shrink batch window to 4ms, (b) prefer stable kernel, (c) pre-reserve KV slab if available. We can A/B roll via canary.

nora: logged perf dump to s3: s3://redwood-inference-debug/1749004321/perf.tar.gz and attached OOM logs to INC. Will follow up with flamegraph later.

samir: thanks. if anyone working on this, ping me before changing batch heuristics globally. small changes can flip latency/cost curve. :eyes:

jia: noted. also adding test matrix across node types (hosted/dedicated/private) to CI so we catch regression earlier.

leo: ok I'll start a small PR with runtime diagnostic and an opt-in longctx policy.

nora: thanks all — I'll keep updates in the incident ticket and drop the flamegraph once processed.
